To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the EDS is a powerful platform for parallel logic program- ming.

(i) the use of a parallel database machine for symbolic processing can be justified, (ii) the shared nothing architecture is the most suitable one, and (iii) a parallel symbolic machine should be designed as a multiprocessor with distributed memory.

The EDS machine architecture, which was designed for high speed data/knowledge base processing, has proven to be a very good platform for the development and evaluation of parallel logic programming languages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the implementation and exploitation of a parallel logic programming system on a shared nothing multiprocessor.
the design of a high performance, parallel information server, for use with declarative languages, such as Prolog.
the development of a parallel machine for the execution of logic programs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EDS project has been very successful.
the EDS is the first system to provide a fully distributed implementation of a parallel logic programming language.
the EDS project has been a success in that it has provided a solid foundation on which to build a parallel information server.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed, built and evaluated a complete parallel logic programming system.
we have developed a complete software system for the EDS, which is currently running on a 16 processor EDS.
we have successfully implemented a prototype of a parallel logic system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the shared nothing architecture, which is a well known and understood architecture for imperative programming languages, is equally applicable to declarative programming languages.
the EDS architecture, which was designed for the development of parallel logic programs, can be applied successfully to the development of parallel object oriented programs.

it is possible to build a shared nothing parallel machine that supports the execution of logic programs and other declarative languages, with a performance competitive with that of a shared memory multiprocessor.
